cohort: Women of reproductive age (15 to 44 years old) diagnosed with obstructing ureteral stones and urinary tract infection
finding: Pregnant women with obstructing ureteral stones and urinary tract infection were 38% less likely to undergo decompression and had greater odds of delayed decompression and longer hospital stays compared to non-pregnant women.
mod_finding: Delayed decompression in pregnant women was associated with increased rates of C-section, early or threatened labor, fetal distress, and umbilical cord complications.
